claim: Introducing weak quenched disorder (random transverse field h_i drawn from U[-W, W] with W << J) into the critical Ising Hamiltonian used in our MERA simulations will NOT improve holographic force signal quality and may degrade it. Liang (PAPER-2026-042) demonstrates MBL protection of holographic geometry in random tensor networks (RTN), but RTN geometry is disorder-native — the randomness IS the geometry. Our MERA geometry, by contrast, is built from a variational ansatz optimized for a clean critical Hamiltonian. Adding disorder shifts the ground state away from the critical point (our MERA was optimized for J=Omega=1 criticality), which we already know (from HYP-2026-010 testing) causes erratic transport and degraded holographic signal. Specifically: at W=0.1J the energy error will increase above our 0.15% baseline at 16q chi=3, and the force profile will show a noisier power-law fit (larger error bars on alpha). The MBL stabilization mechanism in Liang requires tuning to the MBL phase (W >> J), which is incompatible with criticality.
confidence_rationale: HYP-2026-010 testing (mass detuning scan) already demonstrated that departures from criticality in our Hamiltonian cause erratic holographic signal degradation, not improvement. MBL requires strong disorder (W ~ J or larger), which is far from our critical operating point. The RTN vs MERA distinction is fundamental: RTNs gain geometry from disorder; MERA gains geometry from variational optimization. Medium confidence because we have not explicitly tested disorder in the force-profile context (only transport), and it is possible that weak disorder (W << J) improves holographic quality via a different mechanism than MBL.
test_design: 1. Take the 16q chi=3 MERA from SIM-2026-015 (0.15% energy error baseline). 2. Add disorder term: H_disordered = H_critical + sum_i h_i * Z_i, where h_i ~ U[-W, W]. Test at W = [0.05J, 0.1J, 0.2J, 0.5J]. For each W, run 5 disorder realizations (different random seeds). 3. For each realization: (a) Re-optimize MERA (VQE) on the disordered Hamiltonian. (b) Measure energy error relative to exact GS. (c) Compute force profile at dr=1..8. Fit power law, extract alpha and fit error. 4. Average alpha and energy error over realizations. Compare to W=0 baseline. 5. If energy error increases monotonically with W and alpha uncertainty increases, the hypothesis is supported (disorder hurts). If energy error decreases at small W, the hypothesis is refuted.
refutation_criteria: If weak disorder (W=0.05J) reduces energy error below 0.15% or tightens the alpha uncertainty below the W=0 baseline, the hypothesis is refuted and MBL-like stabilization at small disorder is operating in the MERA. If disorder at W=0.1J keeps energy error below 0.5% AND the force signal remains detectable, disorder-stabilized MERA is worth pursuing.
hardware_required: Local GPU (RTX 4060, WSL2) for 16q chi=3 disorder sweep. ~4-8 hours for 5 realizations at 4 W values. No quantum hardware needed for this simulation.
feasibility_notes: 20 VQE runs on local GPU (RTX 4060, WSL2). Each chi=3 16q run is ~400s (from SIM-2026-015 timing). 5 realizations * 4 W values = ~9h total GPU time. Disorder implementation is a one-line Hamiltonian modification. scipy.sparse eigsh used for exact GS comparison. No new circuit code needed beyond SIM-2026-015 VQE framework. This is straightforward local simulation.
philosophical_implications: This hypothesis addresses a fundamental question about the ontology of holographic geometry: is it fragile (requires precise tuning to a critical point) or robust (can be stabilized by multiple mechanisms including disorder)? If confirmed (disorder degrades holographic signal), it supports the view that holographic geometry in MERA is a critical-point phenomenon — a fine-tuned emergent structure that exists only at the quantum phase transition, not a generic property of entangled systems. This aligns with the holographic interpretation of criticality: the CFT on the boundary requires exact conformal symmetry, and any explicit symmetry breaking (by disorder or detuning) generically destroys the conformal structure and with it the AdS dual. If refuted (weak disorder improves or preserves holographic geometry), it would suggest that MBL-like mechanisms can protect holographic geometry beyond the critical point — a more robust and physically interesting picture in which emergent gravity does not require fine-tuning. Liang's RTN result (PAPER-2026-042) would then have a genuine analogue in variational MERA, connecting two previously distinct mechanisms for holographic geometry emergence.

The audit flags this in section 6.3 as a verdict standing on a test that was not executed. CONFIRMED_ANALYTIC is therefore written as a strictly weaker status than CONFIRMED: it records that a perturbative argument was constructed and came out as predicted, and that the 20-run disorder sweep specified in this record's own test_design (W = 0.05/0.1/0.2/0.5 J, five realizations each, ~9h local GPU) was NEVER performed. The refutation_criteria above are stated entirely in terms of measured energy errors and measured alpha uncertainties; none of those quantities was measured. This hypothesis has not been through its own registered test.

It is cheap by this program's standards (~9h on the local RTX 4060), needs no new code beyond a one-line Hamiltonian modification, and would convert an analytic expectation into a measurement. Until then CONFIRMED_ANALYTIC should not be quoted as a numerical result.
